subject: electrical-engineering
intro: Electrical engineering leads to the people who move electrons for a living — designing everything from power grids and electric machines to the chips, amplifiers and control loops inside modern devices.

roles.title: Electrical Engineers
roles.what: Research, design, develop, test or supervise the manufacturing and installation of electrical equipment, components or systems for commercial, industrial, military or scientific use.
roles.where: Units one to six are the core: DC and AC circuit analysis, electronic devices and amplifiers, digital logic, electromagnetics and the power systems unit on transformers, motors and generators are the daily bread of this role.

roles.title: Electronics Engineers, Except Computer
roles.what: Research, design, develop or test electronic components and systems, designing circuits for fields such as telecommunications, aerospace guidance and propulsion control, acoustics, or instruments and controls.
roles.where: The electronics unit on diodes, BJTs, MOSFETs and operational amplifiers, plus signals and systems — Fourier and Laplace transforms, sampling and aliasing — feed directly into the circuit and instrumentation design you would own.

roles.title: Electro-Mechanical and Mechatronics Technologists and Technicians
roles.what: Operate, test, maintain or adjust unmanned, automated, servomechanical or electromechanical equipment, and assist engineers in testing and designing robotics equipment.
roles.where: Digital systems and microcontrollers from the logic unit, feedback and stability from the control unit, and sensors and uncertainty from measurement give you the mixed hardware-and-software fluency this hands-on role demands.

roles.title: Electricians
roles.what: Install, maintain and repair electrical power, communications, lighting and control systems in homes, businesses and factories, working to code and from diagrams to keep current flowing safely.
roles.where: Circuit analysis — Ohm and Kirchhoff's laws, phasors and impedance — plus three-phase power and transformers from the power systems unit explain exactly the systems you will wire, test and sign off.
